situation:
You are the general manager of MERIDIAN STAGE AND RENTAL, an event rental and staging company that supplies portable stages, lighting, and crews to outdoor events across the region. The owner (judge) bought the company eighteen months ago after two losing years and has been turning it around since.

The turnaround has worked so far because the owner (judge) runs a crew on site nearly every weekend, which holds labor costs down and keeps clients happy but leaves no one working on the business itself — no planning, no new accounts, and no schedule for the marketing communications the company has not sent in two years.

The city arts council stood by the company through the two losing years, and the owner (judge) gave the council a written commitment to hold the company's only stage inventory for its summer series weekends. That commitment is the reason the council kept booking while the company was failing.

A regional festival promoter has now offered a season-long contract covering every one of its outdoor stages — enough revenue to buy a second stage inventory and hire a crew chief, so the owner (judge) could stop running crews and start working on the business. The festival dates fall on the same weekends as the council's summer series, so signing means telling the arts council its stages will not be there and breaking the written commitment.

The second inventory's start-up cost would also have to be paid before the first festival payment arrives. Turning the festival down keeps the commitment, but leaves the company at one inventory, sends the contract to a competitor for the season, and keeps the owner (judge) on a crew every weekend. The owner (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the owner (judge) of MERIDIAN STAGE AND RENTAL. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You bought the company eighteen months ago after two losing years and you have worked a crew nearly every weekend since. You want to hear whether the general manager recommends signing the festival promoter's season-long contract or holding the written commitment you gave the city arts council, and you want to hear how that decision would be explained to the arts council.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: How would you tell the arts council what we have decided?
What would you want the council to hear from us first?
